g.text: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged
as a powerful paradigm for improving the reasoning capabilities of
large language models (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025; Shao et al.,
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=2) Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025; Shao et al., 2024).

g.text: Unlike reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) (Ouyang
et al., 2022), which relies on learned reward models, RLVR
leverages rule-based verification of outputs—such as checking
mathematical correctness or code execution—to provide…
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=1) Unlike reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) (Ouyang et al., 2022), which relies on learned reward models, RLVR leverages rule-based verification of outputs—such as checking mathematical correctness or code execution—to provide training signals.

g.text: This approach has enabled substantial improvements in mathematical
reasoning, with models like DeepSeek-R1 (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025)
demonstrating that RLVR can unlock emergent reasoning behaviors.
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=1) This approach has enabled substantial improvements in mathematical reasoning, with models like DeepSeek-R1 (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025) demonstrating that RLVR can unlock emergent reasoning behaviors.

g.text: Scaling RLVR training requires efficient utilization of compute resources.
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) Scaling RLVR training requires efficient utilization of compute resources.

g.text: Off-policy training, where rollout generation is decoupled from
policy updates, offers significant throughput advantages by
enabling asynchronous data collection (Yu et al., 2025).
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) Off-policy training, where rollout generation is decoupled from policy updates, offers significant throughput advantages by enabling asynchronous data collection (Yu et al., 2025).

g.text: However, this introduces staleness: the policy used for rollouts
may be many iterations behind the current training policy.
g.title: N6 [Context] (cites=0) However, this introduces staleness: the policy used for rollouts may be many iterations behind the current training policy.

g.text: Under high staleness, the distribution mismatch between rollout
and training policies creates severe optimization challenges.
g.title: N7 [Context] (cites=0) Under high staleness, the distribution mismatch between rollout and training policies creates severe optimization challenges.

g.text: PPO clipping ineffective; IS variance high
Standard methods like PPO clipping (Schulman et al., 2015) become
ineffective when the policy ratio stays near 1.0 due to stale
data, while importance sampling corrections can introduce
g.title: N8 [Context] (cites=1) Standard methods like PPO clipping (Schulman et al., 2015) become ineffective when the policy ratio stays near 1.0 due to stale data, while importance sampling corrections can introduce prohibitive variance.

g.text: Recent work has proposed various mechanisms to address off-policy
g.title: N9 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Recent work has proposed various mechanisms to address off-policy instability.

g.text: MIS-PO (Huang et al., 2026) applies binary accept/reject masks
based on importance ratio bounds, filtering trajectories that
deviate too far from the current policy.
g.title: N10 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) MIS-PO (Huang et al., 2026) applies binary accept/reject masks based on importance ratio bounds, filtering trajectories that deviate too far from the current policy.

g.text: M2PO (Zheng et al., 2025b) constrains the second moment of
g.title: N11 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) M2PO (Zheng et al., 2025b) constrains the second moment of importance ratios to control variance.

g.text: However, these methods rely on fixed hyperparameters that may not generalize
across different staleness levels and training stages.
g.title: N12 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, these methods rely on fixed hyperparameters that may not generalize across different staleness levels and training stages.

g.text: In our experiments with staleness s = 256, Fixed MIS-PO with default bounds
crashed at step 94 due to gradient explosion, GRPO failed to learn (0% on
AIME benchmarks), and M2PO achieved only 18.40% average accuracy.
g.title: N13 [Result] (cites=0) In our experiments with staleness s = 256, Fixed MIS-PO with default bounds crashed at step 94 due to gradient explosion, GRPO failed to learn (0% on AIME benchmarks), and M2PO achieved only 18.40% average accuracy.

g.text: We propose Acceptance-Controlled MIS-PO (AC-MIS-PO), a method that
adaptively adjusts trajectory filtering bounds based on a target acceptance
g.title: N14 [Method] (cites=0) We propose Acceptance-Controlled MIS-PO (AC-MIS-PO), a method that adaptively adjusts trajectory filtering bounds based on a target acceptance rate schedule.

g.text: Rather than fixing bounds a priori, AC-MIS-PO uses quantile estimation and
exponential moving average (EMA) smoothing to discover appropriate bound
g.title: N15 [Method] (cites=0) Rather than fixing bounds a priori, AC-MIS-PO uses quantile estimation and exponential moving average (EMA) smoothing to discover appropriate bound magnitudes automatically.

g.text: The acceptance schedule starts permissive (40%) and gradually tightens
(20%), allowing efficient learning early in training while maintaining
stability as the policy diverges from rollout data.
g.title: N16 [Method] (cites=0) The acceptance schedule starts permissive (40%) and gradually tightens (20%), allowing efficient learning early in training while maintaining stability as the policy diverges from rollout data.

g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) We identify that bound magnitude is the primary driver of stable off-policy RLVR training. Tighter trajectory bounds that filter more aggressively yield +12.76 percentage points improvement over default MIS-PO bounds.

g.text: We propose AC-MIS-PO, an adaptive controller that targets

automatically discovering appropriate bound magnitudes without
g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) We propose AC-MIS-PO, an adaptive controller that targets acceptance rate using quantile estimation and EMA smoothing, automatically discovering appropriate bound magnitudes without manual tuning.

g.text: We demonstrate that AC-MIS-PO achieves 32.57% average accuracy on
mathematical reasoning benchmarks (Math500, AIME24, AIME25) under
staleness s = 256, outperforming Fixed MIS-PO (18.67%), M2PO
g.title: C3 [Contribution] (cites=0) We demonstrate that AC-MIS-PO achieves 32.57% average accuracy on mathematical reasoning benchmarks (Math500, AIME24, AIME25) under staleness s = 256, outperforming Fixed MIS-PO (18.67%), M2PO (18.40%), and GRPO (6.57%) while maintaining training stability.
